rationale: Although the record concerns community water and sanitation facilities (public toilets and common toilet complexes) in slums (C1 met) and barriers to safe access/use (C4 plausibly met), the explanatory factors explicitly identified in the abstract are physical, spatial, and infrastructural (lighting, location, route, toilet block infrastructure, and number of toilets) driving gender-based violence and crime against women, with no legal, administrative, regulatory, tenure, tariff, or institutional governance mechanism examined (fails C2; primary exclusion code E03). It is also unclear from the abstract whether the paper reports primary empirical data or a general narrative overview (C3 unclear).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Both the narrow rule-type reading and the literal plain reading of Criterion 2 result in exclusion because the abstract examines physical, spatial, and infrastructural hazards affecting women's personal safety (toilet block infrastructure, route lighting, dangerous siting, number of toilets, and usage timings) rather than any legal, administrative, institutional, regulatory, or governance mechanism.

evidence_quotes.quote: The paper focuses on the safety of women in slums in accessing sanitation facilities.
These factors are related to the infrastructure of toilet blocks, the location of the toilet, the route to the toilet, timings of toilet use, and the number of toilets.

The study found that most cases of violence or crime against women are due to a lack of lighting in and on the route to access sanitation and water facilities, lack of access to the toilet block, as well as the dangerous location of PTs (Public Toilets) and CTCs (Common toilet complexes).
